note: Native copy/alloc bounded by an untrusted length: the memcpy/strcpy family, buffer sizing, and binding-layer copies. Every cell below is DOCUMENTED-ONLY (needs_local_verification) — bounds bugs are target facts; grep hits are candidate sites, never proven reachability. Vendor patch-diffing (T-0014's method) is how the real invariant gets pinned per target.

sinks.name: memcpy(dst, src, n) / memmove / bcopy
gates: n attacker-influenced or derived from a protocol field; the vendor patch usually adds the missing bound — diff affected vs fixed builds

sinks.name: strcpy / strcat / sprintf family
gates: no bound parameter at all — the classic unbounded copy

sinks.name: alloca / variable-length array sized by input
gates: the stack-exhaustion sibling of the same invariant

verified.source: C standard library semantics (ISO C99 §7.21.2/7.21.6) and vendor advisories

sinks.name: std::memcpy / std::copy into a raw buffer
gates: same untrusted-length invariant as C; std::copy hides the memcpy spelling

sinks.name: std::string::assign / resize / append sized by external input
gates: allocation-size DoS flavor; native write needs a raw-buffer target

sinks.name: char buf[N] + memcpy from protocol field
gates: fixed-size destination is what makes the length 'unchecked'

sinks.name: FFI::memcpy / FFI cast onto a C buffer
gates: requires the FFI extension enabled — rare in shared hosting; native surface by construction

sinks.name: str_repeat / substr sized by attacker input
gates: heap-exhaustion flavor; memory_limit converts the write into a DoS, not corruption

verified.source: PHP FFI docs and memory_limit semantics

sinks.name: ctypes.memmove / ctypes.memcpy
gates: raw pointer target required — a ctypes buffer is the native surface

sinks.name: bytearray(n) / bytes * k with attacker n
gates: allocation-size exhaustion; corruption needs the ctypes layer

sinks.name: Buffer.allocUnsafe(n) / buf.copy with attacker size
gates: uninitialized memory exposure (allocUnsafe) is the adjacent read-side bug; write side needs a typed-array target

sinks.name: buf.write(str, offset, length) with protocol length
gates: bounds enforced by Buffer in modern node — the bug class lives in native addons (N-API)

sinks.name: FFI::Library / memcpy via ruby-ffi
gates: native surface exists only when a gem binds C — check the Gemfile

sinks.name: String#setbyte / String#* sized by input
gates: MRI bounds-checks these — corruption routes through the FFI layer

verified.source: ruby-ffi documentation and MRI String semantics
